drafted_from: tool:click-on-this-macs-screen row in tools/drive-the-screen/tool-rows.json, read-data/drive-the-screen.mjs (clickOnThisMacsScreen), read-data/hard-deny.json and test/click-on-this-macs-screen.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "In Notes, click New Note." It runs tool:click-on-this-macs-screen once with action click, app Notes and target New Note, and says what changed, with a capture identity from before and after.
no_lists_because: It names no list: it does one thing on the screen when run and answers what it did; workflow:do-a-thing-on-the-macs-screen keeps the record of a longer job.
instructions: 1. The app that runs tools on this Mac needs Accessibility (to read and click) and Screen Recording (for the captures) in System Settings, Privacy & Security; without them the tool answers the permission it needs in `permission` and does nothing. The person turns them on; an AI never does.

2. Your AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:click-on-this-macs-screen and input {action, app, target?, text?, keys?, dry_run?}. action is open, click, type or press_key.
3. Describe the target by what it is called (a label, or { match: { role: "button", label: "Save" } }); a point { at: { x, y } } from a fresh look is the fallback.
4. Read the answer: dispatched, what changed (`effect`), `captures.before` and `captures.after` (BLAKE3 identities of the screen), and `verified` when `expect` was given.
5. A refusal with `refused_by_rule` is final: Privacy & Security panes, password fields, payment confirmations and authentication sheets are the person's own hands. Tell the person what to do there.

worked_examples.title: Click a named button in a named app
worked_examples.given: From tools/drive-the-screen/test/click-on-this-macs-screen.test.mjs (the screen program stood in for): Notes has a button described New Note at 20,20 sized 40 by 20; the captures before and after differ.
worked_examples.hands_back: dispatched true, targets.target {label "New Note", x 40, y 30}, captures {before {blake3 ...}, after {blake3 ...}}, and what changed in `effect`.

worked_examples.title: A click aimed at Screen Recording is refused
worked_examples.ask: Turn on Screen Recording for the app that runs my tools.
worked_examples.given: From the same test: the request names System Settings and a Privacy & Security pane, so read-data/hard-deny.json rule privacy-and-security-settings matches before the screen is read.
worked_examples.hands_back: refused_by_rule "privacy-and-security-settings" and error "Refused by rule privacy-and-security-settings: That is in System Settings' Privacy & Security, where Mac permissions are given. An AI never gives itself or any app a permission; the person does it with their own hands. Nothing was done."
